## Purpose

The package includes YAML templates for the three supported model families.
These templates are the recommended starting point for experiment-level work:
copy one, edit the values, validate it with `read_experiment_spec()`, and run it
with `run_experiment()`.

The compact templates are deliberately small. They are useful for smoke tests,
reviewer checks, and learning the shape of the specification.

| Model | Compact template |
| --- | --- |
| Discrete-time LV | [`lv_discrete.yaml`](https://github.com/opetchey/community.simulator/blob/main/inst/experiment_templates/lv_discrete.yaml) |
| Continuous-time LV | [`lv_continuous.yaml`](https://github.com/opetchey/community.simulator/blob/main/inst/experiment_templates/lv_continuous.yaml) |
| Continuous-time consumer-resource | [`consumer_resource.yaml`](https://github.com/opetchey/community.simulator/blob/main/inst/experiment_templates/consumer_resource.yaml) |

The rich templates show fuller experiment specifications, including treatments,
replicates, interaction or resource-use options, output controls, and parallel
settings.

| Model | Rich template |
| --- | --- |
| Discrete-time LV | [`lv_discrete_rich.yaml`](https://github.com/opetchey/community.simulator/blob/main/inst/experiment_templates/lv_discrete_rich.yaml) |
| Continuous-time LV | [`lv_continuous_rich.yaml`](https://github.com/opetchey/community.simulator/blob/main/inst/experiment_templates/lv_continuous_rich.yaml) |
| Continuous-time consumer-resource | [`consumer_resource_rich.yaml`](https://github.com/opetchey/community.simulator/blob/main/inst/experiment_templates/consumer_resource_rich.yaml) |

## Copy A Template

After installing the package, locate a bundled template with `system.file()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
template <- system.file(
  "experiment_templates/lv_discrete_rich.yaml",
  package = "community.simulator"
)
```

For a ready-made experiment folder, use `setup_example_experiment()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
setup_example_experiment(
  experiment_folder_location = tempdir(),
  experiment_name = "lv_discrete_review",
  example_experiment_name = "lv_discrete_rich"
)
```

Then run the copied YAML specification with `run_experiment()`.


## Optional compiled continuous-time RHS

Both continuous-time models accept `simulation.ode.rhs`. The default is `r`,
which keeps the reference R derivative and existing numerical settings.
To use the C derivative, add:

```yaml
simulation:
  ode:
    rhs: compiled
```

The direct simulator functions also accept `rhs = "compiled"`. Installing the
package requires a normal R-compatible C compiler toolchain. A request for the
compiled RHS fails explicitly if the package DLL is unavailable; it never falls
back silently. The selected RHS is recorded in the experiment specification log
(including the implicit `r` default) and preflight summary. Runtime estimates
are still based on the existing reference calibration.

The solver, tolerances, time grids, output validation and clipping are shared.
Temperature uses deSolve forcings with the selected `linear` or `constant`
interpolation, `rule = 2`, and `f = 0`; endpoints are held. Duplicate times are
averaged and inputs sorted as in the R reference. Pulse immigration remains a
solver event. State finiteness, blow-up and derivative finiteness checks run
inside C on every RHS evaluation, with the same messages as R. LV negative
internal trials are counted in C and returned in `ode_negative_trials` using
the same fields. Returned-state negative and non-finite checks remain in R.

### Parameter vector layout

Each solve sends one double vector to `cs_initmod`. Matrices are flattened in
R column-major order (species index varies fastest). In the following table,
fields appear in packing order; scalar fields have length one.

| Model | Ordered fields |
|:--|:--|
| Consumer-resource | `S`, `R`, prepared immigration, blow-up threshold, `a_u_ij` (S×R), `u_opt_ij` (S×R), `sd_u_ij` (S×R), `resource_use_ij` (S×R), `h_ij` (S×R), `e_i` (S), `d_i` (S), `rho_j` (R), `K_R_j` (R) |
| LV | `S`, `0` (resource count), prepared continuous immigration (zero for pulses), blow-up threshold, prepared growth offset (`1e-6 * rate_scale`), `alpha_ij` (S×S), `b_opt_i` (S), spread (`sd_perf_i`, falling back to `s_i`; S), `a_b_i` (S), `a_d_i` (S), `z_i` (S) |

The lengths are `4 + 5*S*R + 2*S + 2*R` and `5 + S*S + 5*S`, respectively.
Rates and immigration are prepared in R exactly as for the reference; C does
not rescale them again. C allocates parameter and CR uptake storage dynamically
with `R_alloc` inside the solver call. Storage is reclaimed on return or error,
and there is no fixed richness cap. Callbacks use process-local pointers, so
solves must be serial within a process; the package's process-based parallel
workers each have independent storage. No analytic Jacobian is supplied.

The reproducible developer benchmark is `scripts/benchmark_compiled_rhs.R`.
Run it from the repository root against an optimized installed package, rather
than the debug DLL produced by `devtools::load_all()`.
